t: The capital of Bhutan is Thimphu.
Dzongkha is the national language of Bhutan and is written in a script derived from Tibetan.
Gross National Happiness is Bhutan's development philosophy. It values the wellbeing of people alongside economic growth.
Bhutan is a constitutional monarchy. The king is called the Druk Gyalpo. He is Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck, king since 2006 and crowned in 2008.
Paro Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest, is a famous monastery built on a cliff above the Paro valley.
The currency of Bhutan is the ngultrum, linked in value to the Indian rupee.
Bhutan is a landlocked country in the eastern Himalayas, between India and China.
Bhutan is a small country of about 38,000 square kilometres with fewer than one million people.
Archery is the national sport of Bhutan.
The national dress is the gho for men and the kira for women.
The Bhutanese flag shows a white dragon. Bhutan is called Druk Yul, the land of the Thunder Dragon.
Tshechu are religious festivals with masked cham dances, held in dzongs and temples across Bhutan.
Vajrayana Buddhism is the main religion of Bhutan.
Bhutan's constitution requires that at least sixty percent of the land stays under forest.
Punakha Dzong stands where the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers meet. Punakha was the capital of Bhutan until the 1950s.
Tashichho Dzong in Thimphu houses the government offices and the throne room of the king. The Buddha Dordenma statue overlooks the city.
Bhutan became a democratic constitutional monarchy in 2008, when its first national elections were held and its constitution was adopted.
Ema datshi, made with chillies and cheese, is the national dish of Bhutan.
Gangkhar Puensum, about 7,570 metres high, is the highest mountain in Bhutan and is still unclimbed.
Paro has the only international airport in Bhutan. Drukair is the national airline.
Bhutan Time is six hours ahead of UTC.
Ugyen Wangchuck became the first king of Bhutan in 1907, starting the Wangchuck dynasty.
A dzong is a fortress-monastery that serves as both a religious and administrative centre for a district.
Bhutan's national animal is the takin, the national bird is the raven, the national flower is the blue poppy and the national tree is the cypress.
Black-necked cranes spend the winter in the Phobjikha valley near Gangtey, and the people welcome them with a festival.
Bhutan joined the United Nations in 1971.
The Queen of Bhutan is Jetsun Pema. She married King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck on 13 October 2011 in Punakha.
The king and queen have a son, Crown Prince Jigme Namgyel Wangchuck, born in 2016.

Jigme Singye Wangchuck was the fourth king, reigning from 1972 to 2006. He introduced Gross National Happiness and gave the throne to his son in 2006. His birthday, 11 November, is a national holiday.
Bhutan has had five kings: Ugyen Wangchuck (1907), Jigme Wangchuck (1926), Jigme Dorji Wangchuck (1952), Jigme Singye Wangchuck (1972) and Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck (2006).
Tshering Tobgay became Prime Minister of Bhutan in January 2024. The prime minister leads the government, while the king is head of state.
Bhutan has no president. The head of state is the king, and the prime minister leads the government.
Bhutan's Parliament has two houses: the National Council with 25 members and the National Assembly with 47 members.
Bhutan is an independent, sovereign country and is not part of India. It has never been colonised.
Bhutan borders only two countries: India to the south, east and west, and China's Tibet region to the north. Nepal and Bangladesh are close but do not share a border with Bhutan.
Bhutan is divided into 20 districts, called dzongkhags.
Bhutan's National Day is 17 December. It marks the coronation of the first king in 1907.
Gelephu Mindfulness City is a planned special administrative region in southern Bhutan, announced by the king in December 2023.
Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal arrived in Bhutan in 1616. He unified the country in the 17th century and built many of its dzongs.
Guru Rinpoche, also called Padmasambhava, is honoured in Bhutan for helping bring Buddhism to the Himalayas in the 8th century.
The Je Khenpo is the chief abbot and spiritual head of Bhutan's Buddhist monastic body.
Trongsa Dzong is the largest dzong in Bhutan. The first two kings ruled from Trongsa before becoming kings.
Bumthang is a group of valleys in central Bhutan, often called the spiritual heartland of the country.
Rinpung Dzong stands above the town of Paro and is the home of the Paro monastic body and district administration.
Paro Taktsang sits about 3,120 metres above sea level. The temple complex was built in 1692 at the place where Guru Rinpoche is said to have meditated.
Buddha Dordenma is a giant gilded Shakyamuni Buddha statue above Thimphu. It is 51.5 metres tall and was completed in 2015.
Thimphu is famous for having no traffic lights. Police officers direct traffic by hand.
Bhutan's national anthem is Druk Tsendhen, which means the Thunder Dragon Kingdom.
The Bhutanese flag is split diagonally. The yellow half stands for royal authority and the orange half for Buddhist spiritual tradition.
The four pillars of Gross National Happiness are sustainable development, environmental conservation, preservation of culture and good governance.
The fourth king introduced the idea of Gross National Happiness in the 1970s, saying it matters more than Gross Domestic Product.
Hydropower is Bhutan's largest export, and most of the electricity is sold to India. Tala is its biggest hydropower plant at 1,020 megawatts.
Television and the internet reached Bhutan in 1999, when the fourth king allowed them.
Public education in Bhutan is free, and English is the main language of instruction in schools. The Royal University of Bhutan is the national university.
Basic healthcare is free for people in Bhutan, and traditional Bhutanese medicine is offered alongside modern medicine.
Suja is traditional butter tea, and ara is a homemade rice or grain spirit. Both are common at celebrations.
Other popular Bhutanese foods are momos, red rice, kewa datshi made with potatoes, and phaksha paa made with pork.
Men wear a scarf called the kabney with the gho, and women wear a shoulder cloth called the rachu with the kira. Driglam Namzha is the traditional code of etiquette.
The Black-necked Crane Festival is held every year on 11 November in the Phobjikha valley at Gangtey Monastery.
The Paro Tshechu is held in spring, and the Thimphu Tshechu is held in autumn. The Punakha Drubchen and Tshechu take place in late winter.
Besides archery, Bhutanese enjoy khuru, a traditional outdoor dart game, and football.
Bhutan's international telephone code is +975.
Besides Dzongkha, people in Bhutan speak languages such as Sharchopkha (Tshangla) and Nepali. English is widely used in schools and government.
The official name is the Kingdom of Bhutan. Bhutanese call their country Druk Yul, meaning Land of the Thunder Dragon.
Kadrinche or Kadrinche la means thank you in Dzongkha. Kuzuzangpo la means hello.
Tashi delek is a Dzongkha blessing wishing someone good luck and good fortune.
Most visitors need a visa and must pay a Sustainable Development Fee per night. The rate has changed over time, so check the Department of Tourism for the current amount.
The ngultrum (Nu, BTN) is pegged one to one with the Indian rupee, and rupees are also accepted in Bhutan.
Bhutan's climate ranges from subtropical in the southern plains to cool temperate in the central valleys and alpine in the high north. The monsoon brings heavy rain from June to September.
Important rivers include the Wang Chhu through Thimphu, the Paro Chhu, the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu at Punakha, and the Mangde Chhu.
Gangkhar Puensum is the highest unclimbed mountain in the world. Climbing mountains above 6,000 metres has been banned in Bhutan since 2003.
Bhutan banned the sale of tobacco in 2004 and has restricted plastic bags to protect its environment.
Dochula Pass lies at about 3,100 metres on the road between Thimphu and Punakha. It is known for its 108 memorial chortens.
Bhutan opened to foreign tourists in 1974.
Bhutan's national bird is the raven, its national flower is the blue poppy and its national tree is the cypress.
